html:
Decree 770 was a law issued by Nicolae Ceaușescu's government in October 1966 that banned abortion in Romania, with few exceptions, to raise the birth rate.

Abortion had been the main form of birth control, and contraception was hard to get. The births doubled the next year, and children born then were called decreței. Doctors and women faced prison, and women were checked at work for pregnancy. Thousands of women died from illegal abortions, and Romania had the highest maternal death rate in Europe. Many unwanted children ended up in state orphanages, whose terrible conditions shocked the world after the revolution. Abortion was made legal again on 26 December 1989, one of the first acts of the new government of Romania.
sum: Decree 770 was a law issued by Nicolae Ceaușescu's government in October 1966 that banned abortion in Romania, with few exceptions, to raise the birth rate.
